title: Voting-Theory Condorcet Analysis of LLM Juries: When Does Homogeneity Break the Jury Theorem?

original_idea.body:
# Voting-Theory Condorcet Analysis of LLM Juries

On labeled binary safety judgments, estimate per-model accuracy and pairwise vote-correlation, then compare actual majority-vote accuracy against the independent-voter Condorcet prediction to quantify the independence penalty from homogeneity. Inference + voting statistics.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 4: strong chain — quantifies how homogeneity erodes LLM-jury oversight guarantees, a recognized scalable-oversight aggregation pathway.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 5: estimate accuracy + pairwise correlation, compare to Condorcet prediction; ideal for a stats background.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 5: tightly scoped single experiment (independence penalty quantified) with clear success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: public models + labeled data, no internal access, oversight-design relevant.

novelty.reasoning: Empirical Condorcet-degradation analysis for LLM juries under homogeneity appears largely novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: No known empirical Condorcet independence-penalty study for LLM juries.
